parameters.command:
# NOTE: every SSH node in this workflow is a PLAIN command, not an n8n
# expression. Docker's --format uses Go templates written with double braces,
# which n8n would try to evaluate as its own expression syntax and blank out.
# So paths are computed here in shell and handed on through a date file.
#
# Date must be IST. `date` on the host with TZ set is correct by construction -
# no UTC-vs-IST trap like the one that made Exit Sync a day late.
set -u
export PATH=/Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH
DATE=$(TZ=Asia/Kolkata date +%F)
STAGE="/Users/admin/backup-staging/$DATE"
rm -rf /Users/admin/backup-staging; mkdir -p "$STAGE/docker" "$STAGE/native"
mkdir -p /Users/admin/backup-staging
echo "$DATE" > /Users/admin/backup-staging/.date
INV="$STAGE/INVENTORY.tsv"
printf 'kind\tname\tsource\tarchive\n' > "$INV"

# ============================================================
# DISCOVERY - nothing below is a hardcoded service list.
# Anything you add later is picked up because it is derived from
# what Docker actually has, not from a list someone must remember
# to update. That was the flaw in the first version of this job.
# ============================================================
BINDS=/tmp/_bk_binds; PROJDIRS=/tmp/_bk_projdirs; VOLS=/tmp/_bk_vols
: > $BINDS; : > $PROJDIRS; : > $VOLS

for c in $(docker ps -aq); do
  cname=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Name}}' "$c" | sed 's#^/##')
  proj=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null)
  wdir=$(docker inspect -f '{{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project.working_dir"}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null)
  img=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null)
  printf 'container\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$cname" "${proj:-standalone}" "$img" >> "$INV"
  docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{if eq .Type "volume"}}{{println .Name}}{{end}}{{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null >> $VOLS
  docker inspect -f '{{range .Mounts}}{{if eq .Type "bind"}}{{println .Source}}{{end}}{{end}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null >> $BINDS
  [ -n "${wdir:-}" ] && echo "$wdir" >> $PROJDIRS
done

# Volumes that exist but are attached to nothing still hold data - catch them too.
docker volume ls --format '{{.Name}}' >> $VOLS
# Compose projects that are not running right now would otherwise be invisible.
ls -d /Users/admin/*/docker-compose*.y*ml 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 dirname 2>/dev/null >> $PROJDIRS

sort -u $VOLS | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' | grep -v '^$' > /tmp/_bk_vols_u
sort -u $BINDS | grep -v '^$' | grep -vE '^/(var|run|proc|sys|dev)(/|$)' > /tmp/_bk_binds_u
sort -u $PROJDIRS | grep -v '^$' > /tmp/_bk_projdirs_u

echo "discovered: $(wc -l < /tmp/_bk_vols_u | tr -d ' ') volumes, $(wc -l < /tmp/_bk_binds_u | tr -d ' ') bind paths, $(wc -l < /tmp/_bk_projdirs_u | tr -d ' ') compose dirs"

# ---- n8n logical export (kept first: it is what rescued the 12 workflows) ----
if docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx n8n; then
  docker exec n8n rm -f /home/node/wf.json /home/node/cr.json >/dev/null 2>&1; docker exec n8n n8n export:workflow --all --output=/home/node/wf.json >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && docker cp n8n:/home/node/wf.json "$STAGE/docker/n8n-workflows.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "OK  n8n-workflows.json" || echo "WARN n8n workflow export failed"
  docker exec n8n n8n export:credentials --all --output=/home/node/cr.json >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && docker cp n8n:/home/node/cr.json "$STAGE/docker/n8n-credentials.enc.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    && echo "OK  n8n-credentials.enc.json" || echo "WARN n8n credential export failed"
fi

# ---- volumes ----
while read -r v; do
  [ -z "$v" ] && continue
  if docker run --rm -v "$v":/from:ro -v "$STAGE/docker":/to alpine \
       tar czf "/to/vol-$v.tar.gz" -C /from . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'volume\t%s\t-\tdocker/vol-%s.tar.gz\n' "$v" "$v" >> "$INV"; echo "OK  vol-$v.tar.gz"
  else echo "WARN volume $v failed"; fi
done < /tmp/_bk_vols_u

# ---- bind mounts: stop whichever containers write to the path, then copy ----
while read -r b; do
  [ -z "$b" ] || [ ! -e "$b" ] && continue
  slug=$(echo "$b" | sed 's#^/##; s#/#_#g')
  owners=$(docker ps -q --filter "volume=$b")
  [ -n "$owners" ] && docker stop $owners >/dev/null 2>&1
  if tar czf "$STAGE/docker/bind-$slug.tar.gz" -C "$(dirname "$b")" "$(basename "$b")" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'bind\t%s\t%s\tdocker/bind-%s.tar.gz\n' "$slug" "$b" "$slug" >> "$INV"; echo "OK  bind-$slug.tar.gz"
  else echo "WARN bind $b failed"; fi
  [ -n "$owners" ] && { docker start $owners >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "ERROR could not restart containers for $b"; }
done < /tmp/_bk_binds_u

# ---- compose project dirs (compose files, .env, Dockerfiles, source) ----
# node_modules/.git/data volumes are excluded: reproducible or already captured.
while read -r d; do
  [ -z "$d" ] || [ ! -d "$d" ] && continue
  slug=$(basename "$d")
  if tar czf "$STAGE/docker/proj-$slug.tar.gz" -C "$(dirname "$d")" \
       --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='.git' --exclude='*.tar.gz' \
       "$slug" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'project\t%s\t%s\tdocker/proj-%s.tar.gz\n' "$slug" "$d" "$slug" >> "$INV"; echo "OK  proj-$slug.tar.gz"
  else echo "WARN project $d failed"; fi
done < /tmp/_bk_projdirs_u

# ============================================================
# NATIVE (non-Docker) - Hermes, the invoice parser and the 7 cloudflared
# tunnels are launchd services. The first version of this job did not back
# them up at all; their plists hold the bot token and tunnel tokens.
# ============================================================
tar czf "$STAGE/native/launchagents.tar.gz" -C /Users/admin/Library LaunchAgents >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && { printf 'native\tlaunchagents\t/Users/admin/Library/LaunchAgents\tnative/launchagents.tar.gz\n' >> "$INV"; echo "OK  launchagents.tar.gz"; } \
  || echo "WARN launchagents failed"

# Any dir referenced by a LaunchAgent's ProgramArguments is a live service dir.
for p in /Users/admin/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist; do
  [ -e "$p" ] || continue
  plutil -convert xml1 -o - "$p" 2>/dev/null | grep -oE '/Users/admin/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+' 
done | sort -u > /tmp/_bk_nativedirs
echo "/Users/admin/bin" >> /tmp/_bk_nativedirs
sort -u /tmp/_bk_nativedirs | while read -r nd; do
  [ -z "$nd" ] || [ ! -d "$nd" ] && continue
  slug=$(basename "$nd")
  case "$slug" in local-node|Library|cloudflared-bin) continue;; esac
  if tar czf "$STAGE/native/$slug.tar.gz" -C /Users/admin \
       --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='*.log' --exclude='packages' --exclude='cache' --exclude='plugins' --exclude='rclone' "$slug" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    printf 'native\t%s\t%s\tnative/%s.tar.gz\n' "$slug" "$nd" "$slug" >> "$INV"; echo "OK  native/$slug.tar.gz"
  else echo "WARN native $nd failed"; fi
done

# Docker Desktop's own resource settings - the values that caused the 01-09 outage.
cp "/Users/admin/Library/Group Containers/group.com.docker/settings-store.json" \
   "$STAGE/native/docker-settings-store.json" 2>/dev/null && echo "OK  docker-settings-store.json"

# ---- coverage check: discovered vs captured, so a gap is never silent ----
DV=$(wc -l < /tmp/_bk_vols_u | tr -d ' '); CV=$(ls "$STAGE/docker"/vol-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
DB=$(wc -l < /tmp/_bk_binds_u | tr -d ' '); CB=$(ls "$STAGE/docker"/bind-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
DP=$(wc -l < /tmp/_bk_projdirs_u | tr -d ' '); CP=$(ls "$STAGE/docker"/proj-*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
echo "COVERAGE volumes=$CV/$DV binds=$CB/$DB projects=$CP/$DP"
[ "$CV" = "$DV" ] && [ "$CB" = "$DB" ] && [ "$CP" = "$DP" ] || echo "WARN coverage gap - something discovered was not captured"

DN=$(ls "$STAGE/native"/*.tar.gz 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d " ")
echo "COVERAGE-NATIVE archives=$DN"
[ "$DN" -ge 3 ] || echo "WARN native coverage low - expected launchagents + hermes-native + invoice-parser + bin"
echo "---DOCKER-DONE---"

set -u
DATE=$(cat /Users/admin/backup-staging/.date)
STAGE="/Users/admin/backup-staging/$DATE"
VM=192.168.126.180
mkdir -p "$STAGE/omada" "$STAGE/biomax"
INV="$STAGE/INVENTORY.tsv"

# The VM is a separate host: if it is down this SKIPS rather than fails, so a
# good host backup still reaches the NAS.
if ! ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=8 saleshandy@"$VM" true 2>/dev/null; then
  ping -c 1 -t 2 "$VM" >/dev/null 2>&1     && echo "ERROR .180 is UP but SSH key auth FAILED - omada/biomax NOT backed up"     || echo "SKIP .180 unreachable - omada/biomax not in this backup"
  echo "---VM-SKIPPED---"; exit 0
fi
if false; then
  echo "SKIP .180 unreachable - omada/biomax not in this backup"
  echo "---VM-SKIPPED---"; exit 0
fi

# Deliberately does NOT power the VM off - that is the Friday image job.
# utmctl cannot restart it over SSH, so a daily job must never stop the VM.
# Services are discovered, not listed: a new service on .180 is picked up.
ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 saleshandy@"$VM" 'bash -s' <<'REMOTE'
set -u
rm -rf /tmp/bk && mkdir -p /tmp/bk

sudo -n systemctl stop tpeap 2>/dev/null || echo "WARN could not stop tpeap (needs NOPASSWD sudoers rule)"
tar czf /tmp/bk/omada-data.tar.gz -C /opt/tplink/EAPController data properties 2>/dev/null \
  && echo "OK  omada-data.tar.gz" || echo "WARN omada tar failed"
sudo -n systemctl start tpeap 2>/dev/null || echo "ERROR could not restart tpeap - CHECK OMADA"

# Discover every non-stock enabled unit and back up whatever directory it runs
# from, instead of assuming the biomax-* naming stays put.
systemctl list-unit-files --state=enabled --no-legend --type=service 2>/dev/null \
  | awk '{print $1}' > /tmp/bk/units.txt
cp /etc/systemd/system/biomax*.service /etc/systemd/system/tpeap*.service /etc/systemd/system/omada*.service /tmp/bk/ 2>/dev/null || true
for u in $(cat /tmp/bk/units.txt); do
  systemctl cat "$u" 2>/dev/null | grep -hoE '/home/saleshandy/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+'
done | sort -u > /tmp/bk/servicedirs.txt
while read -r d; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  tar czf "/tmp/bk/svc-$(basename "$d").tar.gz" -C /home/saleshandy \
    --exclude='*.log' "$(basename "$d")" 2>/dev/null \
    && echo "OK  svc-$(basename "$d").tar.gz" || echo "WARN $d failed"
done < /tmp/bk/servicedirs.txt

# biomax.db runs in WAL mode: the main file was 2 days stale while a 4MB -wal
# held the recent attendance rows, so a plain file copy is NOT a safe backup.
# The sqlite3 CLI is not installed on this VM, but python3's sqlite3 module
# ships with Ubuntu and .backup() is a proper online backup.
for db in $(find /home/saleshandy -maxdepth 3 -name '*.db' 2>/dev/null); do
  nm=$(echo "$db" | sed 's#^/##; s#/#_#g')
  if python3 -c "import sqlite3,sys
s=sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[1]); t=sqlite3.connect(sys.argv[2])
s.backup(t); t.close(); s.close()" "$db" "/tmp/bk/${nm}.bak" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "/tmp/bk/${nm}.bak" ]; then
    echo "OK  ${nm}.bak ($(du -h "/tmp/bk/${nm}.bak" | cut -f1))"
  else
    echo "ERROR sqlite online backup FAILED for $db"
  fi
done
echo "DBCOUNT $(ls /tmp/bk/*.bak 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
echo "VM discovered $(wc -l < /tmp/bk/servicedirs.txt | tr -d ' ') service dirs"
REMOTE

scp -o BatchMode=yes -q saleshandy@"$VM":'/tmp/bk/omada-*' "$STAGE/omada/"  2>/dev/null || true
scp -o BatchMode=yes -q saleshandy@"$VM":'/tmp/bk/svc-*'    "$STAGE/biomax/" 2>/dev/null || true
scp -o BatchMode=yes -q saleshandy@"$VM":'/tmp/bk/*.bak'    "$STAGE/biomax/" 2>/dev/null || true
scp -o BatchMode=yes -q saleshandy@"$VM":'/tmp/bk/*.service' "$STAGE/biomax/" 2>/dev/null || true
ssh -o BatchMode=yes saleshandy@"$VM" 'rm -rf /tmp/bk' 2>/dev/null || true

for f in "$STAGE/omada"/* "$STAGE/biomax"/*; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  printf 'vm\t%s\t192.168.126.180\t%s\n' "$(basename "$f")" "${f#$STAGE/}" >> "$INV"
done
NF=$(ls "$STAGE/omada" "$STAGE/biomax" 2>/dev/null | grep -c . )
echo "COVERAGE-VM files=$NF"
[ "$NF" -gt 0 ] || echo "ERROR VM stage produced NO files despite .180 being reachable"
echo "---VM-DONE---"

set -u
DATE=$(cat /Users/admin/backup-staging/.date)
STAGE="/Users/admin/backup-staging/$DATE"

# RESTORE.sh is generated FROM the inventory, not hand-written. If tomorrow's
# backup discovers a new stack, the restore script that ships with it already
# knows how to put that stack back - no one has to remember to edit anything.
cat > "$STAGE/RESTORE.sh" <<'RSH'
#!/bin/bash
# Restore this backup onto a Docker host. Run from inside the backup folder.
# Driven entirely by INVENTORY.tsv, so it restores whatever this backup holds.
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
export PATH=/Applications/Docker.app/Contents/Resources/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH
INV="$HERE/INVENTORY.tsv"
[ -f "$INV" ] || { echo "INVENTORY.tsv missing"; exit 1; }

echo "== volumes =="
awk -F'\t' '$1=="volume"{print $2"\t"$4}' "$INV" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r v a; do
  docker volume create "$v" >/dev/null
  docker run --rm -v "$v":/to -v "$HERE/docker":/from alpine \
    tar xzf "/from/$(basename "$a")" -C /to && echo "  $v"
done

echo "== bind mounts =="
awk -F'\t' '$1=="bind"{print $3"\t"$4}' "$INV" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r path a; do
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$path")"
  tar xzf "$HERE/$a" -C "$(dirname "$path")" && echo "  $path"
done

echo "== project dirs =="
awk -F'\t' '$1=="project"{print $3"\t"$4}' "$INV" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r path a; do
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$path")"
  tar xzf "$HERE/$a" -C "$(dirname "$path")" && echo "  $path"
done

echo "== native services =="
awk -F'\t' '$1=="native"{print $3"\t"$4}' "$INV" | while IFS=$'\t' read -r path a; do
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$path")"
  tar xzf "$HERE/$a" -C "$(dirname "$path")" && echo "  $path"
done

echo "== starting compose projects =="
awk -F'\t' '$1=="project"{print $3}' "$INV" | while read -r d; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  ( cd "$d" && docker compose up -d 2>&1 | tail -2 ) && echo "  up: $d"
done

echo
echo "Done. Check: docker ps"
echo "Standalone containers (ntfy etc) are NOT compose-managed - see INVENTORY.tsv"
echo "  kind=container rows, and re-run their original docker run command."
echo "n8n workflows are INACTIVE after restore - activate once credentials are in."
RSH
chmod +x "$STAGE/RESTORE.sh"
echo "OK  RESTORE.sh (inventory-driven)"

( cd "$STAGE" && find . -type f -print0 | xargs -0 shasum -a 256 ) > "$STAGE/MANIFEST.sha256" 2>/dev/null
echo "taken: $(TZ=Asia/Kolkata date '+%F %T IST')" >> "$STAGE/MANIFEST.sha256"
echo "---RESTORE-BUILT---"
cat "$STAGE/INVENTORY.tsv"

set -u
DATE=$(cat /Users/admin/backup-staging/.date)
STAGE="/Users/admin/backup-staging/$DATE"
NAS=truenas_admin@192.168.126.21
NAS_DIR="/mnt/ikigai-local/share1/Backups/IKI-MAC-27/$DATE"

NEW_DIR="${NAS_DIR}.new"
ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "rm -rf '$NEW_DIR'; mkdir -p '$NEW_DIR'" || { echo "ERROR cannot create NAS dir"; exit 1; }
scp -o BatchMode=yes -q -r "$STAGE"/* "$NAS:$NEW_DIR/" || { echo "ERROR scp failed"; exit 1; }

# Every file must exist remotely at the same byte size. This is the ONLY thing
# standing between a bad upload and deleting the last good backup.
fail=0; checked=0
cd "$STAGE"
for f in $(find . -type f | sed 's#^\./##'); do
  l=$(stat -f %z "$STAGE/$f" 2>/dev/null)
  r=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "stat -c %s '$NEW_DIR/$f' 2>/dev/null")
  checked=$((checked+1))
  if [ -z "$r" ] || [ "$l" != "$r" ]; then echo "MISMATCH $f local=$l remote=${r:-missing}"; fail=$((fail+1)); fi
done
echo "checked=$checked mismatched=$fail"
if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ] && [ "$checked" -gt 0 ]; then
  # Swap only after every file verified. Until this line the previous good
  # backup is still the live one, so a failed run never leaves a gap.
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "rm -rf '$NAS_DIR' && mv '$NEW_DIR' '$NAS_DIR'"     || { echo "ERROR swap failed - new backup left at $NEW_DIR"; echo "---VERIFY-FAILED---"; exit 1; }
  echo "---ALL-VERIFIED---"
  du -sh "$STAGE" | awk '{print "size=" $1}'
  echo "nasdir=$NAS_DIR"
  rm -rf "$STAGE"
  # Prune only now, and only YYYY-MM-DD folders: vm-image/ and any hand-kept
  # copy are never matched.
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "cd '/mnt/ikigai-local/share1/Backups/IKI-MAC-27' || exit 0
    for d in *; do
      [ -d \"\$d\" ] || continue
      echo \"\$d\" | grep -qE '^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\$' || continue
      [ \"\$d\" = '$DATE' ] && continue
      rm -rf \"\$d\" && echo \"pruned \$d\"
    done; echo 'remaining:'; ls -1"
else
  echo "---VERIFY-FAILED---"
  echo "old backups NOT pruned - previous backup still on the NAS"
  echo "failed upload left at $NEW_DIR for inspection"
fi

=set -u
VM="{{ $json.VM_IP }}"

# Clean guest shutdown first so the qcow2 is consistent. Needs a NOPASSWD
# sudoers rule for shutdown on .180 - without it this stops here and the VM
# is left RUNNING, which is the safe direction to fail in.
if ping -c 1 -t 2 "$VM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 saleshandy@"$VM" \
    'sudo -n /sbin/shutdown -h now' 2>&1 | head -2 || true
  for i in $(seq 1 30); do
    sleep 5
    ping -c 1 -t 2 "$VM" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "VM down after $((i*5))s"; break; }
  done
  if ping -c 1 -t 2 "$VM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR VM still up after 150s - ABORTING, not touching the image"
    echo "---ABORT---"; exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "VM already down"
fi

# Let QEMU actually exit before reading the disk file.
for i in $(seq 1 12); do
  pgrep -f QEMULauncher >/dev/null 2>&1 || break
  sleep 5
done
pgrep -f QEMULauncher >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "WARN QEMU still running" || echo "OK  QEMU exited"
echo "---VM-STOPPED---"

=set -u
BUNDLE="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.BUNDLE }}"
TMP="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.TMP }}"
ZIP="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.ZIP }}"
mkdir -p "$TMP"

# Zip the cold bundle. ~5 min for a 14G source; the VM is restarted in the
# NEXT node, before the upload, so downtime is the zip only - not the upload.
cd "$(dirname "$BUNDLE")" && zip -r -q "$TMP/$ZIP" "$(basename "$BUNDLE")" || {
  echo "ERROR zip failed"; echo "---ZIP-FAILED---"; exit 1; }

SZ=$(stat -f %z "$TMP/$ZIP" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
# The real image is multi-GB. Anything under 1G means the source read failed
# (a Full Disk Access problem has caused exactly this before) - refuse to ship it.
if [ "$SZ" -lt 1000000000 ]; then
  echo "ERROR sanity check failed: only $SZ bytes"; rm -f "$TMP/$ZIP"
  echo "---ZIP-FAILED---"; exit 1
fi
echo "OK  zip $(du -h "$TMP/$ZIP" | cut -f1)"
echo "localsize=$SZ"
echo "---ZIP-DONE---"

=set -u
UUID="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.VM_UUID }}"
VM="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.VM_IP }}"

# Restarted BEFORE the upload on purpose: Omada and BioMax come back as soon
# as the zip exists, so downtime is the zip duration, not zip+upload.
# utmctl cannot do this over SSH (OSStatus -1743); AppleScript to UTM can.
osascript -e "tell application \"UTM\" to start virtual machine id \"$UUID\"" 2>&1 | head -2

up=0
for i in $(seq 1 36); do
  sleep 5
  ping -c 1 -t 2 "$VM" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "OK  VM back after $((i*5))s"; up=1; break; }
done
[ "$up" -eq 1 ] || echo "ERROR VM did NOT come back - Omada/BioMax are DOWN"

ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 saleshandy@"$VM" \
  'systemctl is-active tpeap biomax-sync 2>/dev/null | tr "\n" " "' 2>/dev/null || true
echo
echo "---VM-RESTARTED---"

=set -u
NAS="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.NAS_HOST }}"
NAS_DIR="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.NAS_DIR }}"
TMP="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.TMP }}"
ZIP="{{ $('Build Paths').first().json.ZIP }}"

ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "mkdir -p '$NAS_DIR'" || { echo "ERROR nas mkdir"; exit 1; }
scp -o BatchMode=yes -q "$TMP/$ZIP" "$NAS:$NAS_DIR/$ZIP" || { echo "ERROR scp failed"; exit 1; }

L=$(stat -f %z "$TMP/$ZIP")
R=$(ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "stat -c %s '$NAS_DIR/$ZIP' 2>/dev/null")
echo "local=$L remote=${R:-missing}"
if [ -n "$R" ] && [ "$L" = "$R" ]; then
  echo "---IMAGE-VERIFIED---"
  rm -f "$TMP/$ZIP"
  # Only now delete older images. Keeps only this run's zip; anything not
  # named vm-image-*.zip (a hand-kept copy) is left alone.
  ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$NAS" "cd '$NAS_DIR' && for f in vm-image-*.zip; do [ \"\$f\" = '$ZIP' ] || rm -f \"\$f\"; done; ls -lh"
else
  echo "---IMAGE-VERIFY-FAILED---"
  echo "local zip kept at $TMP/$ZIP for manual retry; previous NAS image untouched"
fi
